jobs.description:

**VP, Capital Markets \- Strategy and Performance Management**

  

The Capital Markets Strategy and Performance Management team is part of the Office of Strategic Management (OSM) and works closely with the C\-suite and with senior leaders in Investment \& Corporate Banking as well as Global Markets on top strategic priorities, spanning the end\-to\-end lifecycle –from strategy development and solution prioritization all the way through to implementation. This is a high\-impact, highly visible role at the center of Capital Markets.  



  

The OSM brings together the development and execution of BMO’s overall strategy by deeply integrating strategy and performance management within each business, enabled by strong connectivity of the team to the Operating Group Heads and their leadership teams, Finance, Technology \& Operations, and Corporate Functions.


In recent years, the team’s work has included: business growth initiatives, client coverage strategies, business portfolio reviews, new business entry and go\-to\-market strategies, transformation initiatives, and AI acceleration.  



  

The OSM has a longstanding track record of placing team members in key roles across the organization and is recognized as a strong talent incubator for BMO. As a VP, you will have unique exposure to executives and opportunities to build cross\-bank relationships through working with line\-of\-business and corporate function leadership on developing and delivering the bank’s strategic priorities.  



  

**Core accountabilities**

* Provides strategic input into business decisions as a trusted advisor.
* Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non\-routine.

* Engage stakeholders across Enterprise to gather input / subject matter expertise and align on key insights and decisions to inform strategic planning / priorities.
* Leads the execution of strategic initiatives; assesses and adapts as needed to ensure quality of execution.
* Supports business performance management monitoring and action plan development, to ensure tight alignment between business KPIs (leading / lagging) and enterprise ambitions.
Supports change management activities, ensuring cross business/group coordination and logistical support for the implementation of change.  
* 

**Strategy development accountabilities \- detailed**

* Leverages a consultative approach to developing current state analysis (e.g., fact base, opportunity areas) and recommendations on strategic choices / trade\-offs.
* Recommends business priorities, advises on resource requirements and develops roadmaps for strategic execution.
* Conducts analysis and research to provide context into the current state (e.g., industry trends, benchmarks) and inform future state priorities (e.g., financial modelling, best practices)
* Develops business cases by identifying needs, analysing potential options and assessing expected return on investment.
* Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
* May network with industry contacts to gather and identify competitive insights and best practices.

**Delivery accountabilities \- detailed**

* Leads implementation of strategic initiatives within group and across BMO by partnering with various internal \& external stakeholders as required; complexity of initiatives may vary and usually involve multiple stakeholders across the enterprise.
* Acts as a relationship manager on assigned projects / programs and ensures alignment to overall enterprise and group goals.
* Leads the execution of operational programs; assesses and adapts as needed to ensure quality of execution.
* Defines business requirements for analytics \& reporting to ensure data insights inform business decision making.
* Supports strategy execution by leading transformation roadmaps / programs to ensure disciplined delivery and successful change management.
Collaborates with internal \& external stakeholders to provide business context in the design, develop and implementation of programs \& solutions.  
* 

**Executive support / other**

* Supports C\-Suite on other strategic priorities and ad hoc requests as necessary.
* Operates at a group / enterprise\-wide level and serves as a specialist resource to senior leaders and stakeholders.

* Demonstrated excellence in stakeholder management and organizational effectiveness in complex environments

* Able to manage ambiguity

jobs.title: Regional Financial Director, FP&A
jobs.description:
**Who We Are**



O’Dell HVAC Group is a well\-established HVAC equipment representative, partnering with engineers, building owners and contractors throughout Canada. Our success is fueled by our people\-first culture, where teamwork, innovation and professional growth are at the core of everything we do.

  

Our culture is shaped by our values: **Everyone Cares, Driven to Innovate, Let’s Be Curious, Operationally Nimble, and Leverage Collaboration**. These values guide how we work together, solve problems, support our customers and grow as a team.

  

We are seeking a **Regional Financial Director, FP\&A** to join our team in Burlington, Ontario. Reporting to the SVP, Operations \& Performance, you will partner with senior leadership to guide financial planning, forecasting and business performance analysis,  

turning financial insights into recommendations that support informed business decisions.

  

You will work closely with regional and operational leaders to understand performance, investigate business challenges and identify opportunities to improve profitability, productivity, working capital and long\-term growth. You will also oversee the Regional Controller, supporting accurate financial reporting and strong financial controls while keeping your primary focus on strategic analysis, financial insight and business decision support.

  

What You'll Be Doing


* Lead the annual financial planning and rolling forecasting processes, working closely with operational leaders to develop accurate, data\-driven financial projections.
* Act as a trusted financial partner to the President, SVP, and senior leadership team, providing meaningful financial insights and recommendations to support strategic business decisions.
* Analyze financial and operational performance across business divisions, regions, manufacturers, customers, and projects to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Investigate financial performance challenges, including margin fluctuations, pricing strategies, operational costs, and profitability, to identify root causes and recommend solutions.
* Develop financial models, forecasts, and scenario analyses to evaluate business performance, growth opportunities, and potential risks.
* Evaluate the financial impact of import tariffs, duties, supplier costs, and pricing decisions, recommending strategies to protect profitability.
* Identify opportunities to improve operational productivity, inventory management, working capital, and cash flow.
* Prepare financial business cases and investment analyses for strategic initiatives, including business expansion, new product offerings, staffing, capital investments, and acquisitions.
* Lead executive financial performance reviews, presenting key findings, financial results, forecasts, and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Partner with Sales, Operations, Purchasing, Service, and other departments to understand business performance and support continuous improvement.
* Oversee financial reporting quality and accounting controls through the Regional Controller, providing leadership, guidance, and professional development.
* Collaborate with AIR Corporate Finance and FP\&A teams to ensure alignment with corporate financial planning, reporting standards, and business objectives.
* Leverage ERP systems, Power BI, reporting tools, automation, and emerging technologies to improve financial visibility, reporting accuracy, and overall efficiency.
* Support financial systems improvements, business integrations, and reporting initiatives as the organization continues to grow.
* Monitor the financial outcomes of business initiatives and investments, comparing actual results against expected performance and identifying opportunities for adjustment.

* Post\-secondary education in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Minimum of ten plus (10\+) years of progressive finance experience, with significant experience in senior Financial Planning \& Analysis (FP\&A), commercial finance, or a similar strategic finance role.
* CPA, CFA, MBA, FPAC, or a comparable professional qualification.
* Demonstrated experience partnering with senior executives and operational leaders to provide financial insights that influence business decisions.
* Strong experience in financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, financial modelling, scenario analysis, and business performance reporting.
* Proven ability to analyze complex financial and operational data, identify root causes, and translate findings into practical business recommendations.
* Strong understanding of distribution economics, profitability, pricing strategies, inventory management, working capital, and cash flow.
* Experience analyzing the financial impact of import tariffs, duties, landed costs, and supplier pricing.
* Demonstrated accounting knowledge and experience providing leadership or oversight to accounting professionals or finance teams.
* Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and strong experience with ERP systems and business intelligence tools, such as NetSuite and Power BI.
* Experience working within a large, multi\-regional or multi\-business\-unit organization, ideally with annual revenues exceeding $200 million.
* Excellent analytical, problem\-solving, and organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the confidence to present financial findings and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Ability to work independently, challenge assumptions, manage competing priorities, and collaborate effectively with cross\-functional teams.

jobs.description:
**Director of Finance**

**York Region Children’s Aid Society \| Newmarket, Ontario**

**Lead with purpose. Strengthen our future.**

**Bring your financial expertise, strategic perspective, and entrepreneurial thinking to an organization dedicated to children, youth, and families.**


At York Region Children’s Aid Society (YRCAS), strong financial leadership helps make essential services possible. Behind every budget, technology investment, and operational decision is an opportunity to strengthen how we protect children and youth from abuse and neglect and support their well\-being and best interests.


Working alongside parents, caregivers, and community partners, we deliver equitable, culturally aligned services across York Region. Our diverse, interdisciplinary teams bring fresh thinking to child\-, youth\-, and family\-centred care, supported by a culture of belonging where people are encouraged to contribute ideas and lead within their roles.


As our **Director of Finance**, you will join the Senior Leadership Team and work closely with the CEO and Board to turn strategic priorities into sustainable action. Your portfolio spans **Finance, Information Technology, Property and Facilities, and Procurement**—giving you a significant opportunity to shape the systems, resources, and infrastructure that support our mission.


You will also help build our next chapter: developing a shared services model that brings the Society’s expertise to community partners and creates sustainable service\-based funding opportunities.


If you are a strategic CPA who combines sound stewardship with an entrepreneurial outlook and a collaborative leadership style, we invite you to bring your ideas and experience to YRCAS.

**Your opportunity to make a difference**

**Guide financial strategy and stewardship**


Provide the insight, discipline, and direction that help YRCAS navigate a complex funding environment and plan confidently for the future.

* Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, controllership, auditing, internal controls, and financial risk management.
* Develop short\- and long\-term financial strategies aligned with the Society’s goals, legislation, and Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services requirements.
* Lead and resource the Finance team, strengthening the policies, cost controls, tools, and systems that support informed decisions.
* Direct annual budgeting and financial planning, monitor results, and assess performance against budgets and the long\-term strategic plan.
* Engage and advise the CEO and Senior Leadership Team, Finance Committee of the Board and other board Committees on issues, trends and changes in the funding model(s), provincial activities, and operational impacts as well as on cost and expenditures control/deviations, significant budget variances, and extraordinary financial activity.
* Interpret Ministry funding and reporting guidelines; oversee statutory, Board, and Ministry reporting; and approve financial statements before submission.
* Translate funding model changes and provincial developments into clear advice for the Senior Leadership Team, Board Finance Committee, and other committees, supporting effective fiduciary oversight.
* Administer special funds privately held by the Society, including communications with external sources.

**Strengthen technology and operational infrastructure**


Help ensure our people have secure, reliable, and cost\-effective systems and spaces in which to work.

* Directly manage the IT team in the planning and implementation of enterprise information and telecommunications systems, including equipment, software, network services, and printers and in addressing operational challenges, strengthening access protocols, advising on system design, and maintaining cybersecurity measures.
* Oversee building maintenance, repairs, and renovations, along with premises security and building code compliance.
* Negotiate and review mortgages, leases, and renewals in keeping with the Society’s long\-term plan.

**Deliver value through procurement**


Lead purchasing practices that combine operational value with responsible stewardship of public funds.

* Ensure procurement is transparent, competitive, cost\-effective, and aligned with legislation, policy, delegated authorities, and best practices.
* Oversee vendor selection, contract management, and procurement risk.

**Build shared services for the future**


Bring an entrepreneurial approach to expanding the Society’s contribution to community partners.

* Design, integrate and unify shared service offerings that the Society can offer to external stakeholders and community\-based partners.
* Identify sustainable service\-based opportunities that can generate funding to support programs.
* Work with the Senior Leadership Team to develop and implement service\-level agreements with key stakeholders and community partners to provide operational supports such as payroll, accounting, legal services, human resources, and data analytics that will enhance program funding initiatives.


You will also lead other functions and projects that advance the Society’s long\-term plan.

**What you bring**


You combine financial rigour with curiosity, practical judgement, and the ability to bring people with you. You can explain complex issues clearly, navigate competing priorities, and help diverse teams do their best work.


Your qualifications include:

* Successful completion of a bachelor’s degree in a related field from an accredited educational institution coupled with a professional accounting designation (CPA) that is in good standing as recognized within the province of Ontario.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 278455
  

  

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high\-performing culture.

  

Scotiabank is seeking a transformational senior leader to modernize how technology and cybersecurity risks are assessed across the Bank. Reporting to the Vice President, IT Governance \& Risk Oversight within the Office of the Chief Information Officer, the Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments leads Scotiabank's global first\-line technology and cybersecurity assessment capability relating to the Bank’s Threat Risk Assessments and Vendor Security Review processes.

  

The Senior Director brings the Bank's Threat Risk Assessment and Vendor Security Review processes under one leadership responsibility, creating an integrated approach to assessing internally developed technology solutions and third\-party technology services. Together, these form an integrated Assessment Authority: one first\-line capability for technology and cybersecurity assessment that preserves specialized expertise while introducing common leadership and strategic direction, coordinated intake and triage, consistent assessment methods and risk language, shared evidence and quality principles, reusable platform and security patterns, stronger risk reporting and traceability, modern workflows and structured data, and progressive use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation.

  

This role is broader than traditional assessment delivery. It is an enterprise leadership and transformation opportunity to turn fragmented, document\-heavy processes into an integrated, risk\-based and evidence\-informed assessment lifecycle. It brings together technology risk, cybersecurity, security advisory, third\-party risk, cloud and AI security, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) modernization, adoption of ServiceNow Integrated Risk Management (IRM), data and automation, and leadership of a global team.

  

**You will shape and lead six connected themes:**

  

* **Integrated Assessment Authority:** One accountable leadership model for Threat Risk Assessment (TRA) and Vendor Security Review (VSR), with common direction, methods and risk language across specialized assessment teams.
* **Shift\-left security assessment:** Technology and cybersecurity risks identified and addressed earlier in architecture, design and delivery, when they are least costly to resolve.
* **Platform and application assessment:** A two\-level model that assesses shared platforms once and focuses application and vendor assessments on what is genuinely specific.
* **Evidence\-informed risk decisions:** Risk conclusions grounded in structured, verifiable evidence and consistent rating criteria rather than document volume.
* **Modern workflow, data and automation:** Assessments run through modern ServiceNow IRM workflows, supported by structured data and the progressive use of AI and automation.
* **Portfolio risk insight:** Clear, traceable reporting that surfaces recurring and systemic risks across the Bank's technology and third\-party portfolio.

  

**The platform and application model works at two levels:**

  

* **Horizontal assessments** evaluate common platforms, shared services and approved technology patterns once, so related controls and evidence can be reused.
* **Vertical assessments** evaluate the application, workload, project, vendor or material change, and focus on specific deviations, exposures and residual risks

  

**Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:**

  

* Lead the existing TRA and VSR capabilities under one senior leadership model, preserving specialized expertise while establishing common direction, coordinated intake and triage, and shared standards.
* Define and maintain consistent assessment methodology, risk\-rating criteria, quality requirements, evidence principles and finding taxonomies, aligned to the Bank's technology control objectives and enterprise control library and to recognized frameworks such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF), ISO/IEC 27001 and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).
* Embed technology and cybersecurity assessment earlier in architecture, design and technology delivery, including the Bank's delivery framework, architecture review processes and Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
* Establish reusable security and platform patterns that allow downstream assessments to inherit approved baselines.
* Assess material application\-specific and vendor\-specific risks, including data, identity, integration, architecture, exposure and residual risk.
* Strengthen threat modelling and scenario\-based risk analysis, using recognized approaches such as STRIDE and MITRE ATT\&CK.
* Act as the business owner for the technology\-risk assessment capability within ServiceNow IRM, defining assessment requirements, workflows and data needs while working with the technical platform team, which owns platform configuration and delivery.
* Lead the assessment\-domain transition from legacy processes and repositories into modern IRM workflows, preserving application\-to\-assessment and application\-to\-risk traceability and establishing clear data\-quality requirements.
* Define risk\-based triggers for reassessment following material change, significant vulnerability, control failure or deviation from an approved pattern.
* Establish targeted post\-implementation assurance for selected material controls, using authoritative evidence from accountable control owners and specialist functions.
* Prioritize appropriate AI and automation opportunities across intake, triage, context extraction, pattern matching, assessment drafting, evidence orchestration and portfolio insight, in alignment with the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology\-risk automation initiatives.
* Identify recurring and systemic risks across the assessment portfolio and pr

jobs.title: Director, Talent Management & Workforce Insights
jobs.description:
**Putting people first, every day**  



BDO is a firm built on a foundation of positive relationships with our people and our clients. Each day, our professionals provide exceptional service, helping clients with advice and insight they can trust. In turn, we offer an award\-winning environment that fosters a people\-first culture with a high priority on your personal and professional growth.


**Your Opportunity**

Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer and serving as a member of the HR Leadership Team, the **Director, Talent Management \& Workforce Insights** leads an integrated portfolio spanning Talent Management, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics. The Director sets priorities across the portfolio, leads experienced specialist teams and helps these capabilities evolve to better support the firm’s business and people priorities.  

  

  



Working closely with HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and leaders across the firm, the Director will shape the talent systems, workforce insights, rewards and HR services that help BDO retain its people, create meaningful opportunities for talent, and support the firm’s evolving workforce needs. The Director leads through experienced leaders and is not expected to be the technical expert in every area of the portfolio.

**Portfolio Leadership**

* Lead the Organizational Development, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics portfolio, setting clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success.
* Turn the firm’s people priorities into focused plans and practical outcomes.
* Use workforce data, external information and business context to identify risks and opportunities and provide clear recommendations.
* Connect the work across the portfolio so leaders and employees receive clear and consistent support.
* Review what is working, stop or simplify lower\-value work and improve the portfolio based on evidence and business needs.
Foster strong collaboration across HR so firmwide approaches are practical, consistent and responsive to business needs.  
*

* Strengthen the firm’s approach to Talent Management, with an initial focus on reviewing how performance, talent and succession decisions are supported across the firm.

* Set priorities for the People Analytics team based on the decisions and workforce questions the firm needs to address.
* Work with Finance, HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and other stakeholders to bring together business context, workforce data and external talent\-market information.
Help define how the firm’s workforce insights capability should evolve, including opportunities to make better use of analytics, technology and AI.

**Total Rewards \& Wellbeing**

* Ensure reward programs remain competitive, sustainable and aligned with business priorities, market trends and workforce needs.

*

* Set clear priorities for improving HR processes, systems and services, with a focus on simplicity, consistency and the needs of employees, leaders and HR teams.
* Sponsor practical opportunities to use technology, automation and AI to reduce manual work and improve service delivery.
* Ensure the People Analytics team provides accurate, timely and useful workforce reporting and analysis.

*

jobs.title: AVP, CTR Promo Strategy & Programs
jobs.description:
Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most recognized and trusted companies, with a portfolio that spans retail, financial services, loyalty, petroleum, and real estate. Founded in 1922, CTC includes iconic banners and businesses such as Canadian Tire, SportChek, Mark’s, PartSource, Gas\+, Triangle Rewards, Canadian Tire Financial Services, and CT REIT, supported by a national network of retail and gasoline outlets and tens of thousands of people across Canada.

  

  

CTC’s purpose is simple and enduring: “We are here to make life in Canada better.” The company continues to invest in technology, data, omnichannel capabilities, customer experience, and enterprise transformation while maintaining a strong connection to communities across the country. Leaders at CTC are expected to operate with integrity, build strong cross\-functional relationships, and help advance a culture grounded in accountability, inclusion, innovation, and care for customers, employees, Dealers, franchisees, partners, and communities.

  

  

**About the Role**

The AVP, CTR Promo Strategy \& Programs leads the strategy, planning and performance of CTR promotional programs, translating enterprise strategy into customer\-relevant, financially productive and operationally executable plans. The role owns CTR promotional choices and governance, leveraging AI\-enabled capabilities, while building a high\-performing Promotions team.

  

Accountability spans the weekly promotional program, key promo events, non\-product promotions, and integration with key strategic priorities inclusive of customer\-centric growth, Triangle loyalty, Digital activation, and other key price value initiatives. The mandate is to deliver best in class CTR promotional programs through offer and price selection that strengthens customer value perception and drives key financial outcomes.

  

The AVP translates promo strategy priorities into coordinated delivery plans with strong stakeholder management and customer focus. The AVP leads continuous improvement across the function, strengthening workflows, champions automation, and drives disciplined performance management as the promotional ecosystem evolves.

  

**What You'll Do**

**1\. Lead CTR promotional strategy and deliver performance**

* Translate CTR Promotions strategy into an annual plan, inclusive of being a change agent for the multi\-year price value transformation roadmap as part of True North.
* Set the role, depth, frequency, placement and incentive approach for CTR promotions.
* Balance promo sales, retail margin, net promo return, Triangle value and customer value perception.
* Anticipate and respond to competitive dynamics to direct promotional resources toward higher\-impact events and reduce low\-ROI or duplicative promotions.Own promotional outcomes by driving solid in\-season program communication, risk management, trade\-offs, course correction and executive escalation **.**

**2\. Own CTR promo planning and program decisions**

* Lead product and price decisions for CTR promotional program.
* Own product and price selection for key promotional events \- IEPs, NPP events, Special Print Programs and Grand Openings.
* Manage the CTR promotional calendar and ensure integration across events, categories and channels to maximize business performance and customer impact.
* Align promotional plans to category roles, customer needs, key shopping moments and enterprise priorities.
* Challenge the status quo, ensuring promo plans reflect customer and competitive signals to differentiate in the market.

**3\. Lead CTR promo optimization, governance and performance management**

* Set objectives, constraints and high\-quality business inputs for AI\-enabled pricing and promotion engines.
* Embed enterprise promo guardrails for depth, frequency, placement and incentives.
* Establish planning, in\-season and post\-event operating rhythms with standardized dashboards.
* Reduce exceptions through stronger upfront planning, decision discipline and escalation paths.
* Use post\-event insights to improve future event, item and price decisions.

**4\. Advance AI\-enabled promotional capabilities \& optimization**

* Ensure CTR promo process and team readiness for newly launched price value initiatives under the True North strategy.
* Develop a promo automation roadmap and prioritize enhancements that improve impact and efficiency.
* Provide the CTR business perspective to improve models, tools, guardrails and workflows.
* Champion adoption, change management and new ways of working across the team and partners.

**5\. Lead \& build a high\-performing CTR Promotions organization**

* Set clear roles, priorities, decision rights and accountability across Promo Strategy and Promo Programs.
* Coach leaders and build capability in analytics, insight storytelling, systems thinking and judgement.
* Manage capacity, workload and talent progression while strengthening bench strength.
* Set a performance culture grounded in customer impact, reliable execution, evidence\-based decisions, and continuous improvement.
  

**What You Bring**

* You bring 8\-10 years of progressive leadership experience, leading teams in promotions, pricing, merchandising or retail strategy, with the ability to work collaboratively with senior leaders.
* A degree in business, marketing, operations, supply chain, finance or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
* A proven record of developing business strategies and delivering high\-performing programs and events in a large, complex retail organization, ideally in a multi\-category environment.
* Deep understanding of promotional levers, including offer and price selection, depth, frequency, placement, incentive and loyalty mechanics, and promotional calendar planning.

jobs.title: Technology Program Management, Vice President
jobs.description:

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long\-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.


With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.


Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.


**Summary:**
============

The Vice President manages multiple technology projects and teams, establishes governance and stakeholder communications, coordinates dependencies and resources, oversees schedules and reporting, and provides executive updates on strategy, budgets, risks, controls, and delivery. The role also tracks technology expenditures, manages project budgets and capital investments, negotiates internal resources and vendor proposals, and improves project management processes, tools, training, and methodology  



  

**Education**
-------------

  

* Degree or equivalent work experience equally preferable.
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or related field.

  

**Certifications**
------------------

  

* PMP certification preferred.

  

  

**Work Experience**
-------------------

* + Strong experience within a technology organization in the banking or financial services industries. Regulatory reporting domain exposure is a plus.
* + Demonstrated ability to manage multiple and diverse projects and initiatives, including analytical thinking, planning, prioritizing, problem solving, decision\-making, and carrying out assigned projects and activities with minimal supervision.
* + Successfully managed large\-scale and complex initiatives independently, from start to finish, with a duration of at least six months.

---------------------

* + Enterprise \& Architecture Knowledge: Proficient in process and data modeling, architectural development, and IT planning methodologies. Has extensive knowledge of the enterprise's business and decision\-making processes.

* + Vendor Management \& Negotiation: Negotiates beneficial terms for software and services agreements in support of project delivery.
* + Leadership: Builds, leads, and empowers interdisciplinary, geographically dispersed teams.
* + Continuous Improvement \& Planning: Is planning\- and process\-oriented and introduces new processes or delivery methods as needed.

  

* **Foundational Skills**
-----------------------

  

* + Demonstrates leadership, leads by example, and acts with integrity.
* + Communicates effectively and serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership.
* + Applies analytical and critical thinking, iterative problem\-solving, and sound judgment to identify multiple paths to success in a complex environment.

jobs.description:
Department  

  



Finance  

  



  

Reports to  

  



Chief Financial Officer  

  



  

Base salary  

  



$240,000 – $260,000  

  



  

Bonus  

  



Annual bonus opportunity  

  



  

**Overview**
------------

Our client is a fast\-growing developer, owner and operator of community solar, distributed generation and energy storage assets in the US. They are hiring a Senior Vice President to lead capital formation, structured finance, investment underwriting, capital allocation and financial planning.  

  



Reporting to the CFO, you will build and execute the financing strategies that fund the company's next stage of growth.  

  



**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital markets and capital formation**

* Develop and execute the capital markets strategy with the CFO, CEO and executive leadership team.
* Lead capital raising across project, portfolio, asset and corporate financing structures.
* Evaluate and execute financing options, including:
	+ Construction debt
	+ Term debt and back\-leverage facilities
	+ Tax equity and tax credit transfers
	+ Preferred equity and growth equity
	+ Corporate debt and revolving credit facilities
	+ Joint ventures and portfolio financings
	+ Structured capital solutions and asset\-level refinancing
	+ Other strategic financing arrangements
* Build financing strategies that balance cost of capital, liquidity, execution certainty, covenants, risk allocation and long\-term enterprise value.
* Lead negotiations with commercial banks, institutional investors, infrastructure funds, tax equity providers, private credit providers, investment banks, rating agencies and other capital partners.
* Run financing processes end to end: market engagement, term sheets, diligence, documentation, closing and post\-closing compliance.
* Maintain relationships with existing capital providers and open up new sources of institutional capital.
* Track capital markets conditions, interest rates, lender requirements, tax equity availability, investor appetite and renewable energy financing trends.
* Recommend when to finance, refinance, hold, sell, aggregate or otherwise monetise individual assets and portfolios.

### **Project and portfolio capitalisation strategy**

* Set up a disciplined process for deciding which projects and portfolios to prioritise for capitalisation.
* Assess projects on development maturity, interconnection status, permitting, site control, subscriber readiness, offtake, revenue certainty, construction needs, tax credit eligibility, financing availability and projected returns.
* Work with Development, Project Finance, EPC, Asset Management, Subscriber Management, Legal, Tax, Accounting and Operations to judge project readiness and financing risk.
* Build and maintain a prioritised capitalisation roadmap for the development pipeline and operating portfolio.
* Recommend the best timing, structure and grouping of projects for financing.
* Decide whether projects are financed individually, aggregated into portfolios, placed in warehouse facilities, contributed to joint ventures or funded with corporate capital.
* Weigh how to deploy limited capital across community solar, commercial and industrial solar, standalone storage and hybrid solar\-plus\-storage.
* Identify capital constraints, concentration risks, funding gaps and dependencies that could affect construction schedules or commercial operation dates.
* Recommend corrective actions or alternative structures when projects fall short of capitalisation requirements.
* Monitor capitalised projects against underwriting assumptions, financing milestones, budgets and expected returns.

### **Project underwriting and investment analysis**

* Lead financial underwriting for community solar, distributed generation, energy storage and related investments.
* Set consistent underwriting standards, investment criteria, risk classifications and minimum return thresholds.
* Evaluate project and portfolio economics, including:
	+ Development, construction, interconnection and operating costs
	+ Generation and production assumptions
	+ Subscriber acquisition and management costs
	+ PPA terms and community solar credit values
	+ Renewable energy incentives, Investment Tax Credits and adders
	+ Debt sizing and tax equity economics
	+ Merchant versus contracted revenue exposure
	+ Residual and terminal value
* Assess risks across development, interconnection, permitting, construction, supply chain, revenue, customer concentration, regulation, financing conditions and operating performance.
* Make sure investment recommendations combine quantitative analysis with a grounded view of execution risk.
* Own underwriting templates, approval thresholds, risk methodologies and investment review procedures.
* Compare actual project and portfolio performance with original underwriting, explain variances and recommend corrective action.
* Feed lessons from operating assets and completed financings back into underwriting standards.

### **Financial modelling and sensitivity analysis**

* Provide executive oversight of project, portfolio, financing and enterprise financial models.
* Personally review, modify and challenge complex models, rather than relying on outputs alone.
* Use models to test alternative capital structures, financing terms, project groupings, development schedules and operating assumptions.
* Run sensitivity, scenario and downside analysis on capital costs, interest rates, debt capacity, tax equity terms, tax credit eligibility, construction costs, production, subscriber performance, revenue rates, operating expenses, delays, refinancing and exit values.
* Evaluate IRR, NPV, ROIC, cash yield, debt\-service coverage, leverage and payback.
* Keep models accurate, transparent, auditable and aligned with approved corporate assumptions.
* Set model governance: version control, review standards, ownership and approval protocols.
* Turn complex analysis into concise conclu

jobs.title: AVP, Product Strategy - Autonomous Laboratories
jobs.description:
**Job Description**
-------------------

**About Agilent**

  

Agilent is a global leader in laboratory and clinical technologies, we are passionate about bringing great science to life. We help scientists, researchers, and clinicians address some of the world’s most important challenges across life science research, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, food, environmental testing, and related markets.  



  

Leveraging more than 50 years of expertise, we develop advanced instruments, software, consumables, and services that enable customers to generate reliable scientific results and improve scientific, economic, and operational outcomes. Our global organization combines deep technical expertise with a commitment to quality, innovation, and customer impact. We work collaboratively with our customers on their journey to make a real difference in human lives. Our culture is founded on trust, respect, and uncompromising integrity, and we pride ourselves on being a dynamic and inclusive workplace that empowers employees and fosters innovation.

 **The Role**

  

Agilent is seeking a highly experienced product strategy leader to help define how laboratories will evolve over the next five to ten years and translate that vision into actionable strategies for our businesses and product organizations.


This senior individual contributor works across the enterprise at the intersection of customer insight, science, technology, and business strategy. As a recognized internal expert, you will lead high\-impact, long\-range initiatives, advise senior leadership, and independently solve complex challenges spanning multiple functions with limited support. You will connect external signals and customer needs with business\-group priorities, product roadmaps, and execution.

 **Key Responsibilities**

  

* Assess how AI, automation, robotics, connected instruments, digital workflows, data platforms, and autonomous experimentation could change laboratory work. Identify practical applications in scientific productivity, instrument operation, workflow optimization, decision support, and service; distinguish durable shifts from short\-term technology cycles.
* Evaluate new products, solutions, partnerships, and business models. Develop strategic and financial cases that assess customer value, differentiation, and feasibility; recommend when to build, partner, invest, acquire, or apply existing capabilities differently.
* Develop and continually refine Agilent’s view of Autonomous Labs. Synthesize scientific, technological, economic, and operational trends, including changing workforce models and productivity pressures, into scenarios and implications for our portfolio, business models, and investments.
* Engage scientists, laboratory leaders, executives, key opinion leaders, and strategic customers to understand current operations and emerging needs. Identify workflow bottlenecks, fragmented data, automation gaps, usability challenges, and inefficiencies that span individual instruments or product categories.
* Synthesize customer feedback across markets and businesses into clear problem statements, strategic requirements, opportunity areas, and investment recommendations. Connect market direction, competitive developments, technology adoption, and laboratory economics to customer value and business opportunity.
* Partner with individual business and product groups to translate enterprise insight into specific decisions about what to develop, accelerate, integrate, redesign, partner around, or stop pursuing. Convert recommendations into product concepts, roadmap changes, customer experiments, and investment cases.
* Lead initiatives across product management, R\&D, commercial, digital, service, and business leadership. Align teams around customer problems that cross organizational boundaries and opportunities to combine instruments, software, consumables, automation, services, and data into more complete solutions.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a scientific, engineering, business, or related discipline, or equivalent experience. A PhD, MBA, or equivalent advanced experience is strongly preferred.
* Typically 12\+ years of relevant combined experience across product strategy, product management, scientific research, strategy consulting, operations, technology, business development, or related fields.
* Experience in life sciences, analytical instrumentation, diagnostics, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, laboratory technology, or adjacent markets is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to understand complex markets, translate trends into business strategy, and turn customer insight into product, portfolio, or organizational action.
* A record of delivering results across functions and working credibly with senior business leaders, scientists, engineers, and product teams.

 **Skills and Competencies**

  

* Strategic and systems thinking, with the ability to recognize patterns across markets, customers, technologies, and businesses.
* Scientific and technical fluency, curiosity about AI and automation, and sound product judgment grounded in customer needs.
* Structured problem solving and analytical rigor; ability to turn ambiguous information into concrete decisions and priorities.
* Executive communication, facilitation, and influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority.
* Ability to move between long\-range strategy and practical execution, aligning stakeholders and sustaining follow\-through.

**Additional Details**


This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely.
The full\-time equivalent pay range for this position is $192,864\.00 \- $301,350\.00/yr CAD in Canada, or $236,832\.00 \- $370,050\.00/yr USD in the US, plus eligibility for bonus, stock and benefits. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional f
